concept.name: Disinflation
concept.definition: A decrease in the rate of inflation — prices are still rising, but at a slower pace. It is distinct from deflation, which is an actual decline in the price level.
concept.intuition: Disinflation is easing off the accelerator, not going in reverse: inflation falling from 9% to 3% is disinflation even though everything still costs more than before.
concept.mechanics: Measured as a decline in the 12-month percent change of a price index while it remains positive. It typically follows tighter monetary policy (higher interest rates) or the fading of supply shocks; the 1980s Volcker disinflation and the 2023 cooldown from the June 2022 CPI peak of 9.1% are canonical episodes.
concept.formula: Disinflation: inflation_t < inflation_{t-1} with inflation_t > 0, e.g., CPI 12-month change falling from 3% to 2%.
concept.failure_modes: Disinflation driven by collapsing demand can precede recession or slide into deflation; base effects can also make the inflation rate fall mechanically even as monthly price gains stay firm.
concept.misconceptions: Disinflation does not mean prices are coming down — confusing it with deflation leads to wrong expectations about purchasing power and policy.
concept.example: After CPI inflation peaked at 9.1% in June 2022, the U.S. experienced disinflation through 2023 as the Fed's rate hikes slowed price increases without prices falling.

citations.source: Investopedia — Disinflation: Definition, Causes, and Examples
